title: Major Market Moves for Trend Followers - Systematic Investor 308

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/Major Market Moves for Trend Followers - Systematic Investor 308.docx

speakers: Nick Baltas (co-host, quant/trend-following practitioner; caption spells 'Nick Bolas')
summary:
Aug 2024 Systematic Investor: live debrief of the early-August yen-carry unwind and volatility spike (VIX 16 to 65, Nikkei -12%) for trend followers. Trend index lost about 6% in the month, within normal bounds; discusses speed, risk allocation across asset classes, dynamic sizing, 0DTE options, value-at-risk contagion and correlation externalities.
Main conclusion: reversal after a spike is an expected cost of trend following; design choices (speed, balanced vs unconstrained risk, equity caps) explain manager dispersion.

coverage.note: performance snapshot of indices (Aug 2024); trigger of event: weak US jobs, BOJ hike, Nikkei -12%, BOJ put
structuring the discussion; Monday emotions vs v-shape, 2024 equity strength, matching design choices to investor objectives
VIX 16 to 65, carry unwind, dispersion trades and vol selling losses, skew repricing; Crisis alpha in short supply
trend followers underperformed in sharp reversion; no alarm; Monday was a normal day, rules-based
exposure shifts over summer by sector: bonds flipped long, FX, commodities reversion, equities
what drove returns, bonds low-risk then directional; diversification and number of markets; non-traditional commodities
risk allocation in rates down to 10%; vol scaling vs asset-class balance
balanced asset-class risk vs unconstrained trend; speed short-term vs trend
short-term manager vs short-term trend follower; half-life of SG CTA Trend; true vs false positive Monday
asymmetric look-backs, solvency in drawdowns, impure trend with reversion
speed matters for rates and commodities; Volmageddon 356-day streak; March 2023 comparison
equity vs duration shock dispersion; defending 60/40; replicators vs benchmark; 0DTE options
0DTE hedging, long vol did well, risk parity attribution skepticism; risk management and VaR question
VaR vs expected shortfall; parametric vs Monte Carlo; correlation dynamics and externalities
funding liquidity, overplayed systematic-selling narrative, headlines, outro

completeness_estimate: 0.87 - first reader was thorough on design choices, speeds and the August 2024 event; missed the pre-shock low-correlation setup, look-back vs shock length, bonds as historical driver, intraday momentum, risk-manager framing and the VaR contagion nuance.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: my own Trend barometer uh probably to some people surprise is uh is is is fairly High 52 uh but people have to remember that it uses shorter term uh time frames
claims.claim: A short-horizon trend barometer stood at 52 (fairly high) in the August 2024 reversal because short time frames adapt quickly, while longer trend indices were down.
claims.conditions: short time frames benefited in range/fast reversal

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: beta 50 is down 3.6% for the month uh still up 1.55 for the year stock gen c Index is down 4.45% for the month
claims.claim: As of 14 Aug 2024 CTA indices were down 3.6% (BTOP50), 4.45% (SG CTA), 5.98% (SG Trend) and 0.72% (SG Short-Term Traders) for the month, roughly flat for the year, while MSCI World was +8.2% and S&P 500 +12.4% YTD.
claims.indicator: BTOP50, SG CTA, SG Trend, SG Short-Term Traders, MSCI World, S&P 500

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the central bank is not going to change rates if it upsets the market so this is if anything
claims.claim: The BOJ stated publicly it would not hike if it upsets markets, effectively a BOJ put that enabled the rebound, after a small BOJ hike and weak US jobs triggered the biggest Nikkei daily loss since 1987.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: 2024 as an equity market up until the end of July is almost at the top deile of any year since 1928
claims.claim: 2024 equities to end-July were in the top decile of any year since 1928, so the August drawdown was a reversal of an exceptional run, and trend indices had been outperforming until just before.
claims.indicator: US equity annual return rank since 1928

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: I was kind of having conversation with clients that they would be more like oh we should have like a faster system and then two days later they're like actually it's okay
claims.claim: Investors flip between wanting faster or slower systems within days as the V-shaped dynamics unfold, so system speed should be tied to investor objectives rather than recent price action.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: we saw vix from 16% end of July spiking to 65% int on Monday which is a level we haven't seen since covid and it's now down to 24
claims.claim: VIX spiked from 16 to 65 intraday on 5 Aug 2024 and fell back to 24 within a week, a spike-and-revert profile unfavorable to trend following.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the famous FX Cur start unwinding so some carry losses were incurred by those rotations
claims.claim: The BOJ hike plus Fed cut expectations made dollar/yen less attractive and unwound the FX carry trade, causing carry losses.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: dispersion trades lost money some volatility selling trades did lose money the skew in S&P over know um got repriced
claims.claim: Equity dispersion trades and vol-selling lost money as correlations spiked; S&P skew moved from historic lows to its most attractive level in years, offering re-entry opportunities.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: a massive reversion following a spike this was not the environment during March 2023
claims.claim: Trend followers are hurt by sharp mean reversion after a spike (as in March 2023, Feb 2018 VIX spike, Aug 2024); this cost is part of the exposure and not a sign the strategy is broken.
claims.testable: yes: trend returns after vol spikes

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: Monday was a day like any other day there was nothing unusual from a trend falling perspective
claims.claim: Trend followers operate by rules and treat a crash day as an ordinary day, unlike discretionary or other strategies that see frantic activity; trend gains of one early-year week exceed the loss of the August week.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the strategies came roaring back uh actually almost beginning on that day
claims.claim: After the extreme one-day event of Thanksgiving 2020 trend strategies recovered quickly, showing one-day shocks need not damage trend returns.

correction.issue: Wrong year: the caption says 'Thanksgiving 20121', i.e. late November 2021 (the Omicron Black Friday sell-off), not Thanksgiving 2020.
correction.fix: After the extreme one-day event around Thanksgiving 2021 trend strategies recovered quickly, showing one-day shocks need not damage trend returns.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the vast majority of markets across uh regions and Tenors are long so we long Bor Futures
claims.claim: Trend portfolios flipped from balanced to long across bond markets and tenors between June and early August 2024 after long range-bound markets.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: July was a massive reversion I think bom was down by 4 and a half% GCI was down by 4%
claims.claim: Commodities rallied early 2024 then reversed sharply in July (BCOM -4.5%, GSCI -4%), flipping energy positions, while precious metals longs held.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: what has been driving returns here to date the equity rally the weakening of JPY and maybe some Rising commodity
claims.claim: In 2024 YTD trend returns came from three components: the equity rally, JPY weakening and rising commodity prices, with an uninteresting bond market.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: bonds started representing lower and lower and lower risk over the year just because there was no
claims.claim: Under dynamic risk allocation, bonds received less and less risk in 2024 because they were not trending, then regained direction in August.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the downtrends in some of the Commodities like uh grains um actually um got a
claims.claim: Diversified portfolios were cushioned by grain downtrends and non-traditional commodity trends during July/August, which headlines focused on equities and yen missed.

correction.issue: Mixes speakers: Niels makes the grain-downtrend point; the observation that non-traditional, non-benchmark commodities gained almost every day in August is Nick Baltas's.
correction.fix: Niels: strengthening grain downtrends cushioned diversified trend portfolios in July; Nick: alternative non-benchmark commodities added performance almost daily in August 2024, showing the value of diversification insulated from macro moves.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: return dispersion we're going to be seeing between managers certainly also relates to uh the number of markets you trade
claims.claim: Return dispersion between managers depends on the number of markets traded: managers with few markets are hit and miss on Nikkei/yen exposure.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the risk allocation in rates was basically at the minimum we have seen for some time
claims.claim: With dynamic vol scaling, risk allocation fell to about 10% in rates (from 25% across equities, rates, FX, commodities) because rates did not trend while equities and commodities trended.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the second point and that's the one I have more comments on at least for the recent period is whether even after doing inverse volatility scaling
claims.claim: Dynamic sizing has two layers: vol scaling per asset, and whether to force equal risk across asset classes (e.g. 25% each) or let risk flow to the trending class; the latter caused most dispersion between managers.
claims.testable: yes: simulate fixed vs dynamic class budget

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: if you end up having equities contributing 60% of the loss by design a more balanced allocation between the forest classes would have F better
claims.claim: A balanced asset-class risk allocation would have lost less in August (equities caused 60% of the loss) but would have captured less of the equity trend before; it is a trade-off between forced diversification and conviction in signals.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: I don't believe that short-term Trend following works as well as um medium to long-term Trend following
claims.claim: The host believes short-term trend following works less well than medium to long-term, and index data show SG Trend usually beats the short-term traders index.
claims.indicator: SG Short-Term Traders Index vs SG Trend

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: short-term manager will not get out because the trend changes they'll get out by using a Time based stop
claims.claim: A short-term manager exits by time-based or vol-based rules, not by trend change, so short-term managers are a different methodology from short-term trend followers.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: around a 30mon half lifee on an exponentially weighted moving average basis
claims.claim: The SG CTA Trend index behaves like an exponentially weighted signal with about a 3-month half-life; Quantica showed a roughly 66-day half-life signal correlates highly with the index over 10-15 years.
claims.testable: yes: replicate the index with EWMA

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: A true positive in other words whether Monday was the start of a massive drw down
claims.claim: Faster systems helped on Monday but lost out in the recovery because they cut exposure, while medium-term signals lost more at first and recaptured part later; the gap between speeds closed by week-end, so signal speed outcomes depend on whether the reversal is a true or false positive.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: you can't assume that look backs are are symmetrical applied
claims.claim: Look-backs are not necessarily symmetrical for entry and exit: a slow entry (e.g. three months to build) does not imply slow exits, and managers can design faster reaction in a medium-term system.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: remaining solvent in a drawdown is harder than in an NA move
claims.claim: Assessing strategies should focus on turning points and market rotations and how they preserve capital because one must survive drawdowns to see new highs.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: many managers and there's nothing wrong with that um is not pure Trend anymore
claims.claim: Many CTAs are no longer pure trend, which explains performance divergences; Baltas adds mean-reversion and carry components that helped (e.g. quickly going long Japan after losses).
claims.indicator: trend plus reversion plus carry blends
claims.testable: yes: compare pure trend and blends

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the two asset classes where you saw some differing Behavior specifically around a very shorter term speed and longer term speed
claims.claim: In August 2024 speed mattered most in commodities and rates (no established trends), where shorter speeds did substantially better; equities, credit and FX showed little speed difference.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: if the S&P goes for about 340 days without a 2%
claims.claim: The S&P streak without a 2% drawdown before Volmageddon (Feb 2018) was about 356 days versus 351 days before August 2024; long calm streaks precede vol spikes (rule of thumb offered as a half-joke).
claims.direction: reduce long equities after about 340 calm days

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: equities which is typically the growth risk that becomes the differentiation factor between managers
claims.claim: In Aug 2024 the equity shock differentiated managers (fast/equity-defensive vs medium-term unconstrained), whereas in March 2023 the rates shock hit all trend programs similarly regardless of speed or equity constraints.
claims.indicator: equity exposure caps; two-year Treasury sigma move March 2023

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: what are we trying to defend against if it's a 60/40 portfolio
claims.claim: Defensive trend designs (no long equities) were around 0% month-to-date, so design choices (equity caps, speed, class balance) should be matched to what the investor needs to defend, e.g. 60/40 equity and rates risk.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: there was a big dispersion between replicators and The
claims.claim: Replicator (trend replication) products outperformed the benchmark leading into July 2024 but the gap vanished in the six weeks after.
claims.indicator: trend replicators vs SG Trend benchmark

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: selling volatility in those markets did come at a negative return over the last week
claims.claim: Selling 0DTE volatility lost money in the shock but is no different from selling longer tenors; long-vol and long-gamma holders profited and short correlation/dispersion were hit most.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: hedging a zero day option to me appears to be more challenging
claims.claim: Hedging zero-day options is harder since delta and gamma change quickly intraday, and whether dealers are short or long gamma can amplify or dampen moves; no data show 0DTE drove the event.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: I don't think there was one you know one driver
claims.claim: The sell-off was multi-dimensional (carry unwind, correlation spike, liquidity) and blaming risk parity, vol-targeting and CTAs alone is too simple; a postmortem with data on agents is needed.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: value at risk is just a point in a return distribution
claims.claim: Value at risk is only a threshold; use expected shortfall (conditional VaR) for the loss beyond it, and note that VaR is bounded by historical realizations (parametric or Monte Carlo variants).

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: I think the way I would look into risk management would be more along the lines of correlation
claims.claim: Risk management should foresee correlation spikes and externalities from many investors holding similar portfolios and reacting to the same signals (e.g. FX carry), something VaR cannot capture.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the only thing that goes up in a crisis Nick that's correlations
claims.claim: Correlations rise in a crisis, so back-tested diversification overstates protection.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: funding liquidity is is is is one of those catalysts right to to the extent you cannot level up anymore
claims.claim: When investors cannot lever up (funding liquidity constraint), one or two large moves can produce a vicious circle.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: I cannot see how differently a discretionary manager would act if they hold the Magnificent 7
claims.claim: Blaming systematic rule-followers (risk parity, vol targeting, CTAs) for each drawdown is overplayed since discretionary managers would also cut losses.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: we're talking about the least correlated environment in the US market in equities which was the consequence of high level of concentration
claims.claim: Just before the August 2024 shock US equity correlations were at record lows because returns were concentrated in a few mega-cap AI/tech names; such a low-correlation, high-concentration setup left dispersion and short-correlation trades exposed to a sudden correlation spike.
claims.indicator: US equity implied/realized correlation; index concentration
claims.direction: correlation up sharply from record lows; dispersion trades lose
claims.conditions: high index concentration, crowded dispersion trades
claims.testable: yes - implied correlation index levels before shocks

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: I don't think it's changed Direction frankly from because the move is relatively short in time only for only for Windows exactly
claims.claim: A few-day shock is too short relative to medium/long trend look-back windows to flip equity or yen positions; it mainly causes deleveraging and weaker signal strength while most positions continue, so trend portfolios change little after brief crashes.
claims.indicator: trend signal look-back length vs shock duration
claims.conditions: short sharp shock followed by rebound
claims.testable: yes - simulate signal changes through short shocks

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: historically that was the Big Driver of performance and and and over the last like know a year or [L280] two um it has not been
claims.claim: Bond futures were historically the main driver of trend-following returns, but after 2022 rates stopped trending and contributed little, which changes how a trend book's returns are composed.
claims.indicator: trend P&L attribution by asset class
claims.testable: yes - sector attribution of SG Trend / trend replication

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: Niki for instance there was substantial intraday momentum that took place on Monday and had you been exposed to those intraday moves
claims.claim: On the 5 August 2024 crash day the Nikkei showed strong intraday momentum, so strategies following intraday moves from the open would have profited; the net effect of short-dated option hedging depends on whether dealers are long or short gamma.
claims.direction: follow intraday direction from the open
claims.conditions: crash days with dealer short gamma
claims.testable: yes - intraday momentum returns on high-vol days

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: first and foremost we're Risk Managers that's the part of the of the equation we have some input on we have no say in terms of what performance we can get from the markets
claims.claim: Trend followers should see themselves first as risk managers because they control risk taken but not returns the market offers; many managers have moved from stop losses with static sizing to VaR-based portfolio risk models, raising the worry that common VaR use synchronizes selling.
claims.testable: partly - compare drawdown behaviour of static vs VaR-sized trend books

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: if people follow similar rules this cannot in itself have a I guess a contagion effect except the possibility that losses happen at the same time
claims.claim: Contagion from risk models comes from many investors suffering losses at the same moment and unwinding together, not from the choice of VaR as such; the real question is whether the measure is right and whether people over- or under-react to it.
claims.indicator: VaR / expected shortfall usage across investors
claims.testable: partly - flow data around risk-limit breaches
